title: Nearest Airport Finder: Closest Major Airports
description: Find the nearest major airports to any place with the Nearest Airport finder — distances from a city or your position. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, from central London the list leads with airports approx. 15 miles away at Heathrow — with the City and Gatwick alternatives ranked behind it.
quick_answer: The Nearest Airport finder lists the major airports closest to a place you name or your current position, with the distance to each. Search from a city or your location and read the ranked list — the first step in choosing where a trip actually begins.
steps_intro: Trips begin at an airport, not at a destination pin. Find the right starting point:

body.t: The nearest airport is not always the best airport — but the ranked distances are where the comparison starts. Flight thinking continues in the
“Which airport are you flying into?” deserves a list, not a guess — especially where a metro area has three.
A new city's air links are part of its livability. The nearest major airports, and their distances, are the first paragraph of that research.
In sparse country the answer may be a two-hour drive — better known at planning time than at booking time.
From the centre: Heathrow approx. 15 miles west, London City much closer but limited, Gatwick approx. 28 miles south. The finder ranks them; your airline's network makes the final call.
From Manhattan, LaGuardia is approx. 9 miles, JFK approx. 15, Newark approx. 14 — three majors inside a taxi ride, which is why the question needs a list.

faq: No — it lists major airports, the ones with scheduled flights a traveller can book. Grass strips and private fields are a different hobby's map.
Does the route include live traffic?
No — the distances are geographic. The drive to the airport is a separate, traffic-haunted question for the routing tools.
Why is road distance longer than straight-line?
The airport distances here are point-to-point; the taxi or train journey will be longer. Budget the road figure, admire the straight one.
Can route results change over time?
Airports rarely move; the list changes when new majors open or data improves. Rankings by distance are stable civic facts.
From my exact position or a city?
Either — a named place or your device's position. Position is used to build the list and nothing else.
The one with the flight: distance ranks the candidates, routes and times decide among them.
Majors of both kinds appear; the destination's needs filter the list better than any label.
The nearest airport has no flight to my destination.
Common — proximity ranks, networks decide. Take the list to the flight tools and let routes filter it.
Not in the majors list. This finder serves scheduled-flight travel, where the airport choice actually changes a booking.
